answer: Proof-of-stake mechanisms mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital, creating a high financial barrier to entry. An attacker attempting to simulate a vast juniper or willow network faces the prohibitive cost of acquiring sufficient stake to gain influence. By requiring a verifiable signal of economic commitment, the system ensures that identity proliferation is bound by real-world resources rather than computational output alone, forcing attackers to bear significant risk of asset devaluation.
